headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: Copilot can read repo/editor context while TREK handles secrets and collaborative travel data, creating default-path exposure and unverified downstream use.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads editor buffers and repo context, while TREK is a real-time collaborative app with MCP and WebSocket surfaces. That creates a plausible manual or indirect content bridge, but no shared filesystem or automatic instruction channel is documented, so the injection path is limited and not default-hijack level.
conditions: IF TREK content is copied into Copilot prompts or editor buffers, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF a shared MCP or file bridge is added between the pair, attacker-controlled text can cross agents.
mitigations: Keep TREK outputs out of Copilot prompts unless reviewed.
Disable any shared clipboard or file-sync bridge between the tools.
Use a separate workspace for TREK artifacts.
Add a short prompt-injection checklist before pasting TREK text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for TREK-generated content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and sends context to api.githubcopilot.com, while TREK handles reservations, documents, photos, API keys, and MFA secrets in files and collaborative sessions. Even without a shared workspace explicitly stated, the pair can expose sensitive travel data if TREK material is placed into Copilot context.
conditions: IF TREK reservations, documents, photos, or secrets are pasted into Copilot buffers, they may leave the local environment.
IF both tools are used on the same workstation profile, accidental cross-exposure becomes plausible.
mitigations: Do not paste TREK secrets or reservations into Copilot.
Use separate browser/profile sessions for TREK and Copilot.
Redact API keys and MFA secrets before any AI-assisted editing.
Store sensitive TREK files outside the Copilot workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction on shared editor buffers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state; TREK exposes collaborative files and real-time sessions with MCP. If both operate on the same repo or shared mutable workspace, concurrent edits and state drift are plausible. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository or directory, write conflicts can occur.
IF TREK uses MCP to mutate shared state while Copilot proposes edits, state drift becomes likely.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Require human review before applying Copilot edits.
Pause TREK writes while Copilot is editing the same files.
Use git branches per agent.
requires-engineering: add file-level locking or merge arbitration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces code edits and TREK is a collaborative planner with AI built in; if TREK consumes Copilot-generated text or code as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect plans or actions. There is no documented verification barrier between them, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF TREK ingests Copilot output without verification, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF Copilot-generated edits are copied into TREK workflows, TREK may act on unvetted content.
mitigations: Require a human verification step for Copilot output before TREK uses it.
Mark Copilot text as untrusted in TREK workflows.
Do not auto-import Copilot-generated snippets into TREK.
Use a review-only handoff format.
requires-engineering: add source attribution and validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and user accounts, while Copilot sends context to a vendor API. If regulated travel or identity data is placed into Copilot context, the pair can create a compliance breach by moving sensitive data into a third-party service without a documented residency or retention control. The profiles do not show a mitigating DPA or residency guarantee.
conditions: IF TREK data containing reservations, identity data, or secrets is entered into Copilot, third-party processing occurs.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not provided by Copilot, compliance exposure is triggered.
mitigations: Keep regulated or secret-bearing TREK data out of Copilot prompts.
Use synthetic or redacted examples for Copilot-assisted work.
Review vendor data-processing terms before sharing TREK content.
Separate environments for regulated and non-regulated travel data.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based redaction and residency controls.
